record.summary: Amending law that writes AI into Uzbekistan's Law on Informatization and Code of Administrative Responsibility. It defines artificial intelligence as technological solutions that imitate human knowledge and skills, including independent learning and searching for solutions, and adds Article 7-1: AI-made information resources and AI-based systems must not harm a person's life, health, freedom, honour, dignity or other inalienable rights, and legally significant decisions affecting human rights and freedoms may not rest solely on their conclusions. Unlawful processing of personal data using AI, and its dissemination in the media or online, is fined 50 to 100 base calculation units.
record.notes: Adopted by the Legislative Chamber on 12 August 2025, approved by the Senate on 1 November 2025, signed on 21 January 2026 and in force from its official publication (Article 4), which lex.uz dates 21 January 2026. The amendments also give the competent state body AI tasks: attracting investment in AI, building technical infrastructure to process government data with AI, and training staff. Article 3 instructs the Cabinet of Ministers to bring government decisions into line with the law. lex.uz publishes a Russian text marked as an unofficial translation.

verification.note: Recheck of 17 Oct 2026: re-read the lex.uz Russian page (document 8011377) and the lex.uz English card (document 8011930), both stored on 11 Oct 2026, and stored the official Uzbek text (lex.uz document 8008401, Cyrillic) on 17 Oct 2026. The Uzbek text confirms the title, number, chamber dates, signature, the National Database of Legislation reference of 21 January 2026, entry into force on official publication and the full text of Articles 1-4; the summary now renders its definition of AI. The Russian page is marked 'Неофициальный перевод'; the English card says the text is given in Uzbek and Russian and offers only machine translation, so no English version was found. The archiver flagged the Uzbek page for review because the page title is short; its text is this law. Version 1's first-reading date and the press reports on a labelling duty in the first-reading draft rested on no stored file and were removed; the enacted text contains no labelling provision.

judgment.status_reasoning: Article 4: the law enters into force on the day of its official publication; lex.uz gives 21 January 2026 as the date of entry into force, which has passed. No repeal appears. 'In force' stands.
judgment.scope_reasoning: Amending law whose purpose is to regulate relations arising from the use of AI: a definition, a harm-prevention rule, a ban on decisions resting solely on AI outputs and an AI-specific offence; in scope with no note.
judgment.date_reasoning: date_published is the signing date (21 January 2026), which is also the date of official publication in the National Database of Legislation; the law entered into force that day under Article 4.
